notes.title: Official Wiki
notes.content:
Welcome to Elderfield now has an official Wiki! 

Check it out here

This is just the beginning, as there is still a ton of info to add. I've set up the main pages and navigation, and have populated several of the pages with basic information and layouts.

There is a lot that still needs to be done - if you'd like to contribute to the wiki, read the "Contribute to the Wiki" section at the bottom of the homepage. Anyone can contribute simply by registering.

For those who don't feel comfortable with wikitext, you can click "edit" on many of the pages and sections to add/change basic text without opening the source editor. This way, you can easily add basic info and fix errors etc. without needing to look at anything too complicated.

Be sure to preview any edits you make before saving them. For those who don't know much about wikitext, you can click "Edit Source" on any page/section to see what I have already set up and add your own info in, or you can copy the wikitext from other pages as a starting point.

Feel free to make posts in the Discussions page here or on the Discord with questions if you need help editing the wiki.

You can also make posts requesting certain content or info from me if you need it for editing the wiki (such as game info, images, etc.).

Note that you can view the source of any page on other wikis hosted on wiki.gg as well, and you can copy that source wikitext to use as a starting point for new articles and just change the information. This is a great way to grab layouts that you may not know how to make yourself (such as grabbing tables etc. from other wikis).

You can see a list of other wiki.gg wikis here: https://www.wiki.gg/wikis

Happy editing!

notes.title: The Save-Breaking Update
notes.content:
Well folks, the time is here! It's time to break all of your save files. 

Those who have been following the game's progress will have been expecting this for a while now. It's taken about 6 months to get everything working properly, but it is time to finally give the game's controls an upgrade. 

This update will be dropping soon, so now is your advance notice to disable automatic updates for the game if you don't want these changes. 
That said, if you do accidentally update but want to play your old saves, this is easily fixed (read on). 

This update will not be compatible with saves made on previous versions of the game. That said, you can continue to play your old saves on the previous version of the game. 

If you accidentally update to this version and didn't mean to (ie. Steam auto-update), you can find the last version of the game which is compatible with old saves here: https://welcome-to-elderfield.itch.io/welcome-to-elderfield/devlog/944372/v0133b

If you accidentally updated, just back up your save folder and replace the files in your Welcome to Elderfield directory with the ones in the above itch download (or just move your saves into that folder and launch it from there), then move your save folder back. 
Doing the latter will also have the benefit of having both versions of the game installed, so you can play old saves on that version and make new saves on the current Steam version as well.

This update brings the following changes:

 You can now click near the player to turn and interact with tiles/objects. Clicking far away from the player will still interact with the tile you are already facing.
 A tile outline image now shows which tile you will interact with when the mouse is clicked
 All menus have been reworked to be more mouse-friendly, and gamepad navigation should now be much faster
 Many redundant menu clicks have been removed
 You can now click once to deposit/withdraw an item, sprint+click to deposit a full stack, and ctrl+click to select a quantity
 Item “use” options have been reworked. Many are used instantly when selected (such as food or decorations), and items with no use-able function no longer show a list of options.
 Many item options now have descriptive names such as “Eat” or “View”. 
 Item dropping has been reworked, now requiring sprint+click to choose an amount to discard 
 Visual buttons have been added to the withdraw/deposit/drop scenes for mouse users
 The furnace and grinder now show coal requirements
 Processors will now take coal directly from primary storage

notes.title: Character Customization!
notes.content:
Character Customization is here!

Character customization has been a highly requested feature, and I've always said "probably not, but you never know". 

Well... after a ton of work overhauling how player sprites and animations are handled, and creating hundreds of new individual sprite sheets, character customization is now in the game.

[previewyoutube=RAAUe-6YWpI;full][/previewyoutube]

The reason this feature was such a big "probably not", it mainly due to the engine this game is made in, RPG Maker MZ. While there are plenty of character customization solutions out there for the engine, they are all fairly basic and not very flexible. Welcome to Elderfield has a ton of functionality implemented which the engine doesn't natively support, such as diagonal movement, an animation system with many different player animations, idle animations, multiple different running animations, and so-on. No standard plug-and-play character builder plugin was going to cut it, and it was clear that something more custom would be required. 

And so, after a significant amount of work, I've managed to build my own system for handling character customization. This involves a ton of extremely convoluted event-based system, and the use of a composite bitmap plugin which allows me to create new sprite sheets and images by combining multiple layers. This new customization system tells the game which options you've selected, and then a number of processes run which construct every animation sprite sheet, portrait image, and so-on for every individual tool, walk/run animation, player angle, idle animation, and so-on. 

I'm glad that it ended up working out, but we'll see how well this system holds up. There may be bugs, and who really knows how this is all going to work out. There is always a chance that something breaks and the whole thing needs to be scrapped, so fingers crossed! With limited tools comes a limited ability to fix things, so hopefully it all just plays well with the rest of the game.

notes.title: Major Combat Changes
notes.content:
Here's another update which focuses more on changing some of the core gameplay as opposed to adding new areas/content. 

This update focuses on the combat system, and I've tried to include something to address most common complaints. This wont resolve every issue, however I think it will be a good starting point, and I have many more ideas to keep making combat more interesting. 

CHANGELOG

 Added health bars for enemies
 Added some new "surprises" to Shoppers
 Evasion has been removed. All +/-Evasion modifiers have been replaced with +/-Hit Rate
 Many niche stats have been removed from the status window
 A new "Skills" system has been added for non-magical attacks which use MP
 Added 5 new physical skills (1 starting, 2 vending machine, 2 loot)
 Guard has been changed, and is now a skill which costs MP. It resists the next attack, unless broken by special guard-breaking skills.
 Fixed enemy states not displaying
 Most rituals now deal more damage
 Luck rolls have been changed to be more random, and less influenced by the luck stat
 The wardrobe has been removed
 Equipment can be changed any time
 The hit/miss system has been overhauled, fixing old bugs and allowing for new skill possibilities
 Clearing farm clutter can no longer cause curses. Overall causes less "bad things" to happen.
 Coal rocks now give 2x coal
 The HUD MP bar now moves in the right direction
 Fixed animal friendship meter not displaying correctly

notes.title: The Alpha Demo is Here!
notes.content:
After a year of development, the alpha demo is live! 

NOTE: Steam Deck users may not see the demo button on the store page. Click "Download Demo" on desktop to add it to your library, then launch via Steam Deck.

This demo includes about 1/6th of the final game, and should take between 10-20 hours to complete (depending on how much of a completionist you are). 

This demo includes the core farming mechanics, fishing, some limited animal husbandry, crafting, cooking, and the first "level" of the game's first dungeon, complete with main boss and mini bosses. 

There is also a ton of optional/side content to help you get to the end in whichever way you please, at whatever pace. 

Alpha Stuff

This alpha build has been tested by some very dedicated testers over on our Discord, but I'm sure there will be plenty of bugs to report now that the "real" launch is here, so do not hesitate to report any bug in the community tab or on our Discord. 

This is an alpha, so be sure to save often and in multiple save slots!

Game updates should be compatible with older saves generally, but be sure to check the patch notes when a new update releases to ensure that your save will carry over, and do not be afraid to back up your saves folder just in case - I cannot guarantee anything this early in development, and if I have to break saves to fix something crucial, I will. 

To offset the potential game-breaking and bugs, there is a cheat mode enabled in the difficulty settings which should help you get back to where you were in the event that you do lose a save. 

Feedback and Bug Reports

With this being an alpha demo, feedback is crucial.

Please report ant bugs, but do not hesitate to also give game balance feedback, feature suggestions, and any other feedback you can think of. I will be reading all of it!

Community

As mentioned above, we have a Discord server. 
You can find it on our steam page, and also via an in-game link on the title screen.

We also have a Patreon! 
You can find it in our "website" link on our Steam page. Patreon supporters have access to future development builds of the game beyond the Demo, which will continuously be posted all the way until the final release. Patreon is a great way to support development while also experiencing the game as it comes together in real time. The next major update will double the town size and add a whole new "dungeon" area, so consider supporting the development if you'd like to see what that looks like.
